subject: Quarterly Business Review — launch commitments & delivery triage
messages:
From: Ruth Cohen <ruth@atlas.systems>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver White <oliver.procure@atlas.systems>
Date: 2027-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep — roadmap & commitments

Soojin — thanks for the detailed packet. A couple of asks from our side ahead of the QBR: 

1) Can you confirm the GA date window for the Dedicated offering with the quantized runtime? We need that to align procurement and our SaaS launch.
2) Are there any remaining third-party connector risks (we have a strict compliance window to meet)?

Oliver and I will be on the QBR on May 26; if you can surface the decision matrix, that would help.

– Ruth
Customer Success, Atlas Systems
From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Ruth Cohen <ruth@atlas.systems>, Oliver White <oliver.procure@atlas.systems>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep — roadmap & commitments

Ruth — thanks. Short answers up front: 
- GA window for the dedicated quantized runtime: targeting July 18–25 (can tighten if we de-risk the KV cache work).
- Third-party connector: the OAuth2-based analytics ingest connector has an outstanding cert that may slip one week; not blocking GA if we gate it behind feature flags.

I've attached a one-page decision matrix and the latest roadmap summary (QBR_Roadmap_Summary_v2.pdf). Karthik/Marcus — see the two open risks flagged below that I want triaged before the exec call.

Top risks (summary):
- KV cache invalidation interaction with continuous batching (owner: Karthik) — potential 8–12% tail-latency regressions in 99p under burst.
- Preemptible GPU fallback behavior in the Dedicated pool (owner: Marcus) — could require a canary routing exception to preserve SLAs for key accounts.

Action: please respond with mitigations and whether you’d like these surfaced in the decision slate.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep — roadmap & commitments

Folks — quick status from infra/serving: 
- KV cache invalidation: root cause narrowed to a race during multi-request cache refresh under burst. Mitigation 1: serialize refreshes for hot prefixes (adds ~5ms median). Mitigation 2: optimistic TTL extension + background reconciliation (adds complexity to rollback).
- My recommendation: implement the serialize-refresh fallback for the QBR canary (INF-4521). It’s low-risk and buys us runway to test the background reconciliation for the GA ship.

I’ll attach a short diagram to the Drive folder (KVCache_Risk_Diagram.png). Marcus — I need a decision on whether we run canary traffic from the EU pool as well. That will affect rollout timing by ~72 hours.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep — roadmap & commitments

Agree with Karthik's low-risk approach. Follow-ups: 
- I'll schedule the canary for July 19 with serialized refreshes enabled. We will run a 48-hour burst simulation before gating canary traffic.
- EU pool: do not include in the initial canary. Keep EU for parallel validation to minimize blast radius. That means GA window stays July 18–25 but EU ramp starts +3 days after US GA.

Also calling out a procurement ask: we need Atlas to sign the SLA exception for preemptible-fallback behavior (DocuSign link included). Ruth/Oliver — can you confirm if procurement can execute this by June 7?

Marcus Lin
VP, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Ruth Cohen <ruth@atlas.systems>, Oliver White <oliver.procure@atlas.systems>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep — roadmap & commitments (final pre-read)

Ruth/Oliver — attaching the final pre-read for the QBR and the decision slate (Launch_Decision_Matrix.xlsx). Highlights for the exec pack: 
- GA window: US July 18–25, EU stagger +3 days; contingency lanes defined for OAuth connector and KV cache.
- Recommended exec asks: sign SLA exception for preemptible fallback; approve canary with serialized KV refresh; accept EU staggered ramp.

If procurement can sign the DocuSign by June 7 we’ll ship the first cohort in the July window. If not, we will move the GA out by two weeks to keep the EU parallel ramp intact.

Next steps for QBR: 
- Karthik: one-slide on mitigation timeline (due EOD May 25)
- Marcus: canary schedule + traffic simulation notes (due EOD May 25)
- Laura: exec summary and final slide deck (due May 26 morning)

Thanks everyone — see you in the QBR.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
Attachments: QBR_Roadmap_Summary_v2.pdf, Launch_Decision_Matrix.xlsx
